arguments.value: 12-year-old girl admitted with a few days of burning, itching, genital pain, abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, dysuria, and fever, with inflamed, swollen vulva and bleeding subcutaneous ulcers on the labia minora and lesions involving the labia majora, labia minora, hymenal caruncle, and vestibulum. Labs showed inflammatory changes (leukocytosis, neutrophilia, elevated CRP and procalcitonin); urinalysis showed cloudy dark yellow urine with alkaline pH, protein, WBCs, and abundant bacteria. She was treated with cefuroxime, topical silver sulfathiazole ointment, and NSAIDs; histopathology of ulcerated tissue showed necrotic and purulent lesions without neoplastic process. Symptoms improved, she was discharged after three days, the lesions completely resolved by 60 days, and she remained asymptomatic during one-year follow-up. The ulcers developed about a week after her first BNT162b2 COVID-19 vaccine dose; she later received the second dose without side effects.
